claims_about_writeup.why: A manual word-count of the write-up's text (title, body paragraphs, references line) comes out to roughly 236 words, matching the claimed 239 closely enough given tokenization variance (hyphenated terms, citation punctuation); no material discrepancy.

message_source_quote: WBS (in `papers/`) uses a *think vs don't-think* contrast; this uses a *secrecy / covert-vs-overt holding* contrast
writeup_source_quote: not the think/don't-think contrast of white-bear steering (Raman et al., 2026), which uses the same family

differences.message_quote: the *actual* directed_modulation think-vs-don't-think direction reaches 0.78, matching the white-bear paper
differences.what: The message reveals that a diagnostic was run using the source's own (white-bear) think/don't-think direction and that it reproduced the paper's reported 0.78 result, validating the pipeline against the source; the write-up never mentions this reproduction/validation step.

differences.message_quote: ~9 hand-authored stance contrasts I tried (name-vs-continue, deep-vs-surface, salience, hold-vs-forget, etc.) all degraded pass@10 monotonically — only the "held named concept" axis works, and the novel twist was to take its *secret* pole rather than the don't-think pole
differences.what: The message discloses the exploratory search (nine failed alternative contrasts) that led to the final secrecy-contrast choice and frames the novelty explicitly as swapping the source's don't-think pole for a secret pole; the write-up states the novelty only as a different kind of contrast (secrecy vs. think/don't-think) without describing this search or using this framing.

rationale: Both documents explicitly name and credit Raman et al., 2026 (white-bear steering) as the prior work from which the method's contrast idea departs, and both frame the novelty identically: a secrecy/covert-vs-overt contrast replacing WBS's think/don't-think contrast on the same directed_modulation family. The message, however, adds material not in the write-up: a diagnostic that reproduced the source's own direction at its reported 0.78 score (validating overlap with the source) and a description of nine failed alternative contrasts that motivated the final choice, giving a more detailed account of the method's relationship to and departure from the source than the write-up provides.
